'''Katherine Richardson Christensen''' (born May 11, 1954 in [[Chicago]], Illinois) is Professor in Biological [[Oceanography]],<ref name=":0">{{cite web|url=http://www.science.ku.dk/fakultetet/organisation/ledelse/kr_cv/|title=Katherine Richardson Christensen|publisher=Copenhagen University|accessdate=March 10, 2009|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110716021231/http://www.science.ku.dk/fakultetet/organisation/ledelse/kr_cv/|archivedate=July 16, 2011}}</ref> leader of the Sustainability Science Centre and a researcher for the Center for Macroecology, Evolution and Climate at the [[University of Copenhagen]]. She was the vice dean of the Faculty of Science from 2007–2012. Her research focuses on the importance of biological processes in the ocean for the uptake of carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and how ocean biology, including diversity, contributes to ocean function in the Earth System.

Katherine was one of the main organisers of the scientific conference "[[Climate Change: Global Risks, Challenges and Decisions]]",<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2009/feb/09/scientists-summit-climate-change|title=Scientists plan emergency summit on climate change|last=Adam|first=David|date=February 9, 2009|work=[[The Guardian]]|accessdate=March 10, 2009}}</ref> which sought to inform the [[2010 United Nations Climate Change Conference]].

== Life and work ==
She completed a B.A. at [[Harvard University]] in 1976 and completed a Ph.D. in Marine Science from University of North Wales, UK 1980.<ref name=":0" />

Katherine Richardson was Chairman of the Danish Commission on Climate Change Policy that reported in 2010 and presented a roadmap for how Denmark can become independent of fossil fuels by 2050. She is at present a member of the Danish Climate Council and was a member of the 15-person Independent Group of Scientists appointed by Ban Ki Moon to draft the 2019 UN Global Sustainable Development Report.<ref>{{Cite web|title=GSDR 2019 .:. Sustainable Development Knowledge Platform|url=https://sustainabledevelopment.un.org/gsdr2019|access-date=October 23, 2020|website=sustainabledevelopment.un.org}}</ref> She is Co-Editor in Chief of the ''[[Marine Ecology Progress Series]]'' and a member of the editorial board for ''Global Sustainability''. Authorship of books includes ''Our Threatened Oceans'' (2008)<ref>{{Cite web|title=Our Threatened Oceans – by Stefan Rahmstorf und Katherine Richardson|url=http://www.pik-potsdam.de/~stefan/oceans.html|access-date=October 23, 2020|website=www.pik-potsdam.de}}</ref> with Stefan Rahmstorf and ''Climate Change: Global Risks, Challenges and Decisions'' (2014)<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/climate-change-global-risks-challenges-and-decisions/6799E08D063BC2D88E09697BAD69260D|title=Climate Change: Global Risks, Challenges and Decisions|date=2011|publisher=Cambridge University Press|isbn=978-0-521-19836-3|editor-last=Richardson|editor-first=Katherine|location=Cambridge|doi=10.1017/CBO9780511973444 |editor-last2=Steffen|editor-first2=Will|editor-last3=Liverman|editor-first3=Diana}}</ref> together with Will Steffen, Diana Liverman and others. She is or has been a member or chair of numerous national and international committees and organisations relating to science policy and/or sustainability. She is currently co-chair of the Northern European Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN).
